claims.title: Pairwise controlled stationary laws cancel unknown currents into a weighted diffusion identity
aliases: weighted Fisher identity for stationary SDEs
claims.claim: Let the same smooth unknown drift b and constant symmetric D≻0 govern controlled diffusions on R^d with vanishing boundary flux/integrability, or on a flat torus. Under known smooth controls u_i, strictly positive stationary C² densities p_i and divergence-free currents J_i=(b+u_i)p_i−D∇p_i, set r=p_i/p_j, w=∇log r and δu=u_i−u_j. For every admissible scalar q for which the integrations are justified, the source derives D:E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ]=E_{p_i}[q(r)δu·w]. Thus full rank of the collected symmetric matrix features M_{ij,q}=E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ], in dimension d(d+1)/2, identifies the constant D uniquely.
claims.interface: All regimes share b and constant state-independent D; intervention fields are known; stationary laws are exact and fully observed for the theorem. The feature-rank condition is a hypothesis to check, not a consequence of having multiple regimes. The test-function class for q and the required boundary/integrability conditions are not fully enumerated in the source.
claims.proof_spine: Use J_i=rJ_j+p_i(δu−Dw). Choose f with f′(r)=q(r)/r, multiply the stationary divergence equation by f(r), cancel the J_j term as a gradient against a divergence-free current, and integrate the remaining divergence by parts. The resulting identity is linear in the symmetric entries of D.
claims.costs: No finite-sample or numerical acquisition bound. The features require density-ratio gradients and stationary expectations; acquiring or estimating these, waiting for each regime to mix, and calibrating controls are uncharged. An algebraic perturbation bound is conditional on the exact design singular value and feature errors.
claims.failure: Rank deficiency prevents unique D recovery; two-regime weighted features can be ill-conditioned despite full rank. The exact identity does not supply a statistical estimator for general smooth densities or a physical snapshot-acquisition protocol.
claims.comparator: Fokker–Planck inversion and weak-form/Stein generator identities have established prior work. The source reports a partial literature check and leaves the exact weighted current-cancellation identity priority UNKNOWN.
claims.gate: Independently reconstruct the identity with an explicit admissible q class and boundary conditions; verify the symmetric-feature vectorization and assess exact-identity prior art.
claims.related_scope: No cross-result theorem applicability is asserted.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported independent analytic derivation and finite consistency checks; this intake did not reconstruct the proof or rerun code. External correctness, formal certification, priority and physical validation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale or 9–10/10 breakthrough was established.
claims.unavailable: Exact maximal q regularity class, independent proof review, priority, nonasymptotic sample guarantees and physical acquisition costs remain UNKNOWN.

claims.title: Full generator recovery is conditional on rank, while two stationary laws leave an invisible current
aliases: d plus one controlled stationary densities
two stationary populations cannot identify drift
claims.claim: Let s_i=∇log p_i and T_i=∇²p_i/p_i for d+1 controlled experiments, and define W(x)=[s_1−s_0,…,s_d−s_0]. For i=1,…,d define h_i=D:(T_i−T_0)−∇·u_i−u_i·s_i+∇·u_0+u_0·s_0. Under the source’s smoothness and exact-law assumptions, if the pairwise matrix features identify constant D and W(x) is invertible almost everywhere, subtracting stationary Fokker–Planck equations identifies b(x)=W(x)^{−T}h(x) almost everywhere. Conversely, for a compatible pair of positive stationary densities on T², known D and controls do not identify general b: adding v(x)=p_0(x)^{−1}S∇(p_1/p_0), for a nonzero constant skew matrix S, preserves both stationary laws but changes their currents.
claims.interface: The sufficient theorem assumes full-state, exactly known positive stationary densities, common smooth b, constant D, known controls, full rank in the D-feature system and almost-everywhere pointwise rank of W. The counterexample is on the flat two-dimensional torus and retains the same D and controls. Neither statement is a finite-sample result.
claims.proof_spine: Subtract the stationary Fokker–Planck equations to obtain d linear equations in b(x); invert W wherever it has full rank. For the obstruction, p_0v=S∇r has zero divergence, and p_1v=rS∇r also has zero divergence because S is skew and Hessians are symmetric.
claims.costs: The nonparametric formula uses density scores, second derivatives, pointwise matrix inversion and conditioning. Statistical error, regularization, regions where W is nearly singular, mixing, finite samples and partial observation have no guarantee.
claims.failure: A singular or poorly conditioned W prevents stable drift recovery. The two-regime gauge refutes unrestricted full-drift identification from those two laws, but it does not refute recovery of D or the d+1 rank-conditional theorem. A radial or latent projection does not satisfy the full-state interface.
claims.comparator: The source cites prior Fokker–Planck algebra and intervention-identifiability work; no complete proof-level priority audit is reported. N498 is a useful projection-loss contrast, not a theorem premise.
claims.gate: Independently verify the almost-everywhere uniqueness statement and the two-law gauge for the declared boundary conditions; quantify what changes under partial observation or noisy estimated scores.
claims.related_scope: N498 demonstrates a specified radial observation that hides full-system irreversibility. The present theorem requires full-state observation; this is an interface warning and scoped comparison, not a deduction from N498.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported analytic derivation and synthetic numerical diagnostics; no external proof review, formal verification or physical system identification was performed at intake. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
claims.unavailable: Independent proof correctness, a statistical reconstruction theorem, robustness under noisy/partial observation, and priority remain UNKNOWN.

claims.title: Exact affine density tilts determine diffusion and a nonreversible generator under a full-rank force contract
aliases: B equals U A inverse diffusion symmetric part
claims.claim: On R^d, suppose p_i(x)=Z_i^{−1}p_0(x)exp(a_iᵀx) for i=1,…,d, with A=[a_1,…,a_d] nonsingular, known constant forces U=[u_1,…,u_d], a common drift and constant D≻0. Under consistency and normalizability, the source derives B=UA^{−1}, D=sym(B), K=skew(B), and b(x)=B∇log p_0(x), with stationary current J_i=K∇p_i. Thus an arbitrary nonlinear log p_0 is allowed within this exact-tilt family and the circulation can be nonzero. Fewer than d independent tilt directions cannot guarantee full generator identification in the worst case within the family.
claims.interface: The tilt relation is exact, A is full rank, controls are known constant forces, and D is constant symmetric positive definite. The identification result assumes exact stationary laws; classifier estimates of tilt slopes from independent stationary samples are a separate statistical procedure. Estimating b or entropy production still requires score information.
claims.proof_spine: Use the pairwise identity with q=1 and constant w=a_i−a_j to recover the symmetric part of UA^{−1}; the score-difference matrix is A, so the stationary Fokker–Planck subtraction gives b. Conversely the skew part produces a divergence-free stationary current. If fewer directions are observed, perturb B by a nonzero E annihilating all observed a_i while preserving positive definiteness of sym(B+E).
claims.costs: No finite-sample rate for estimating A, B, D or b is proved. Accuracy depends on force amplitudes, density overlap and conditioning of A; physical preparation of independent stationary regimes and time to equilibrium are not charged.
claims.failure: The formula is specific to exact exponential tilts with invertible A. It does not extend automatically to arbitrary density ratios, unknown/state-dependent diffusion, changing drift across interventions, latent state, or finite-sample high-dimensional estimation.
claims.comparator: The source recognizes OU intervention and broader stationary SDE identifiability literature; exact priority for this nonlinear-base affine-tilt formula is UNKNOWN. The route is a conditional structural result, not a general identification algorithm.
claims.gate: Independently verify both directions of the affine-tilt corollary and the fewer-than-d worst-case intervention obstruction; compare the exact model with prior stationary-intervention results.
claims.related_scope: The source’s affine model can express stationary entropy production after score acquisition, while N186 uses charged trajectory/reversal observations. Their data and assumptions differ; no conversion or theorem composition is asserted.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported written derivation with synthetic diagnostics; this intake did not independently reconstruct or externally review it. Exact-tilt assumptions, sample-access costs and prior-art limits remain explicit. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
claims.unavailable: Independent proof certification, historical priority, finite-sample guarantees and physical acquisition costs remain UNKNOWN.

claims.title: Synthetic stationary-snapshot diagnostics are model-conditional and do not establish physical acquisition
aliases: 3D exact iid density ratio diffusion diagnostics
claims.claim: The packet reports three synthetic diagnostics. In a three-dimensional non-Gaussian quartic exact-i.i.d. tilt model, 25 repetitions at 32,000 accepted draws per regime produced mean relative Frobenius errors 1.70% for B, 1.71% for D and 1.52% for K; local generation/fitting time excludes physical preparation and equilibration. A two-dimensional non-affine torus calculation used deterministic stationary-grid solutions, not random observed samples: at grid side 192, three-regime D error was 0.0288%, while the two-regime weighted system had condition number about 198 and 3.74% error. A quartic-family entropy-production estimate reported 1.63% mean relative error at 32,000 draws per regime over 12 repetitions, with the quartic potential family supplied and an independently sampled reference based on 750,000 additional baseline draws. These are source-reported synthetic outcomes, not empirical scientific validation or finite-sample theorems.
claims.interface: The 3D study uses exact independent synthetic stationary draws and a specified quartic potential; the torus study solves a discretized stationary PDE and computes grid scores/Hessians; the entropy-production study supplies the quartic potential family and draws a separate reference. None uses real physical data or charges physical stationary preparation.
claims.proof_spine: The handoff records generated sample populations, numerical stationary grids, estimates, errors, replication counts and selected controls. The finite proof-check output tests floating-point consistency only. The packet scripts/results are preserved; no script or experiment was rerun during repository intake.
claims.costs: Reported CPU timings omit physical perturbation, calibration, mixing/equilibration and instrument costs; the entropy-production reference uses 750,000 additional exact independent baseline draws (1,050,000 rejection proposals). Grid computation is exponential in dimension. No costed physical or noisy-correlated stationary-snapshot acquisition is demonstrated.
claims.failure: The source explicitly reports model-misspecification, rank/conditioning, score/Hessian acquisition and high-dimensional sample barriers. The two-regime torus estimate is ill-conditioned despite full rank; deterministic-grid precision is not sample-based recovery.
claims.comparator: The 3D finite-force Gaussian-moment comparator is not state of the art. The source separately supplies a stronger same-sample score-moment comparison in N551. No broad estimator dominance or novel physical capability is claimed.
claims.gate: Replicate with independently generated finite noisy stationary data under charged mixing/preparation costs and controlled misspecification; first establish that the needed density-ratio gradients or score structure can be estimated in the intended dimension.
claims.related_scope: No cross-result theorem applicability is asserted; numerical outputs support only the named synthetic setups.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported finite synthetic diagnostics; archive and result records were checked, but scientific code was not executed during intake. No real-system validation, external review, formal verification or historic-scale breakthrough is established.
claims.unavailable: Physical validation, acquisition-complete high-dimensional guarantees, robust misspecification bounds and priority remain UNKNOWN.

claims.title: Supplied-basis weak moments are familiar, and a matched score estimator removes a dominance claim
aliases: weak generator moments supplied drift basis
matched score moment versus density ratio logistic
claims.claim: The packet’s weak stationary-generator regression replaces density derivatives with empirical weak-form generator moments only after supplying an eight-function Fourier drift basis: on its synthetic 2D torus model, 12 repetitions with 80,000 samples per regime (240,000 total) report mean drift-coefficient error 4.01% and D error 5.50%. The source itself demotes this strategy as established weak Fokker–Planck/Stein prior art. In a separate 25-repetition paired same-sample comparison on the 3D quartic model, at 32,000 samples per regime the logistic density-ratio estimate had 1.78% mean B error versus 1.62% for score moments that additionally use the known quartic potential family; the reported paired 95% interval for the logistic-minus-score error difference is [−0.048,+0.360] percentage points and includes zero. The experiments establish no general estimator dominance.
claims.interface: The weak-moment linear system assumes a supplied finite drift basis and known test functions; data are generated by a numerical stationary simulator. The matched comparator reuses the same sample populations, while the score-moment method receives the quartic potential family. Reported intervals describe repetitions of one synthetic distribution, not population-science uncertainty.
claims.proof_spine: Weak integration by parts expresses stationary generator moments using observed positions and known test functions. The paired score-moment comparator uses a_i=−E_{p_i}[∇log p_0] after fitting the supplied-form quartic potential. The source reports errors and comparison intervals, but this intake does not independently run either method.
claims.costs: The finite drift basis and quartic family are supplied structural information. The simulations omit physical acquisition and equilibration. No nonasymptotic guarantee, real-data confirmation, or broad efficiency comparison is given.
claims.failure: Without the basis or potential-family information, the source’s shortcuts do not solve generic high-dimensional score acquisition. The weak method is prior art, and the score estimator sometimes outperforms the logistic estimator; do not claim a new dominant algorithm.
claims.comparator: The source cites published weak Fokker–Planck/Stein methods and a matched same-data parametric score-moment comparator. This card records an explicit prior-art demotion and negative dominance result, not a novelty claim.
claims.gate: Verify the matched information sets and uncertainty calculation, audit the cited weak-form prior art, and require an acquisition-complete comparator before claiming algorithmic advantage.
claims.related_scope: No cross-result theorem applicability is asserted. The reported comparator only applies to its stated synthetic quartic model and matched sample populations.
claims.status_boundary: Source-reported synthetic computation and prior-art assessment; no scientific code was executed during intake. Weak-form methods are acknowledged prior art, and no estimator dominance or historic-scale result is established.
claims.unavailable: External replication, broad matched comparisons, source-family-free acquisition and publication priority remain UNKNOWN.
